# 04 — Asset, licence, AI-use and originality compliance

## Asset strategy

**Goal: zero third-party art, audio or fonts.** Everything visible or audible is generated by the
team's code at runtime.

| Category    | Plan                                                                                                                     | Credit-list entry                          |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Graphics    | Canvas 2D vector drawing in code                                                                                         | "Original, procedurally drawn by the team" |
| Music / SFX | WebAudio synthesis in code                                                                                               | "Original, synthesised at runtime"         |
| Fonts       | System font stack only                                                                                                   | "System fonts; none bundled"               |
| Icons       | Hand-written inline SVG paths                                                                                            | "Original"                                 |
| Libraries   | Svelte, SvelteKit, Vite, adapter-static (all MIT)                                                                        | Name, URL, licence (MIT)                   |
| Dev tooling | TypeScript (Apache-2.0), Vitest (MIT), Playwright (Apache-2.0), ESLint (MIT), Prettier (MIT), Tailwind CSS if used (MIT) | Name, URL, licence                         |

If any external asset is added later: record source URL, creator, licence, download date and a
licence screenshot in `docs/licenses/` **at the moment it is added**.

AI-generated images or audio: **not planned.** If that changes, log the tool, prompt, date and the
tool's commercial-use terms per asset.

## AI use policy for the team

1. AI tools (Claude Code) may draft code, tests and docs.
2. **Every AI-authored change is reviewed by a named team member before merge**, and that person must
   be able to explain it. Use the AI to explain code, but the human signs off.
3. Keep `docs/AI_USE_LOG.md` updated daily (template below).
4. Never paste personal data, credentials or other teams' material into an AI tool.
5. Commit messages note AI assistance (e.g. a `Co-Authored-By:` line).

### `docs/AI_USE_LOG.md` template

```markdown
| Date       | Tool / model                  | Purpose                    | Files / assets affected     | Human reviewer | Review notes / changes made      |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 2026-10-01 | Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) | Scaffold + fixed-step loop | src/lib/game/client/loop.ts | <name>         | Read, tested on phone, renamed X |
```

### AI Use Declaration (draft wording for the portal)

> AI tools used: Claude Code (Anthropic). Purpose: pre-production planning documents (September),
> and AI-assisted code, tests and documentation during 1–31 October. Affected: most TypeScript/Svelte
> source files. See docs/AI_USE_LOG.md for per-file detail. No AI-generated art, music, voice or
> other media: all graphics and audio are procedurally generated by our own code. Human review:
> every change was reviewed, tested and approved by a team member before merge; the team can explain
> and maintain all submitted code.

## Originality declaration notes (fill in truthfully at submission)

- The concept and design documents in `preproduction/` were written before 1 October. **Disclose
  this.**
- All submitted code, levels and assets are created in the competition repository between 1 and 31
  October. The commit history is the evidence.
- A pre-competition technical prototype existed and **was not reused**. Disclose per the
  organizer's answer to the question in `00_RULES_AND_RISKS.md` §3.
- Genre acknowledgement (optional but honest): "Inspired by the time-loop cooperation genre; no
  levels, art, code or text from other games were used."

## README template (`README_TeamName_GameTitle.md`)

Must cover the guide's 17 items:

1. Game title · 2. Team name · 3. Main contact · 4. Short description · 5. How to open and play
   (URL + local: unzip, serve folder) · 6. Supported browsers (Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari, current) ·
2. Supported devices (Windows, macOS, Android 10+, iOS 16+) · 8. Controls & gameplay · 9. Known bugs
   / limitations (or "None") · 10. Third-party tools/libraries · 11. Asset credit summary · 12. Special
   testing instructions (e.g. "Level select unlocks sequentially; press ⟲ to end a loop early") ·
3. Recommended orientation/resolution/aspect (landscape, ≥ 640×360, 16:9–20:9) · 14. Internet /
   external API requirements: **None** · 15. AI tools, purpose, affected code/assets · 16. Private repo
   access instructions + submission commit/tag · 17. Build version / release identifier.

## Technical notes (portal) — draft

> Static HTML5 Canvas 2D game built with Svelte 5/SvelteKit (adapter-static). No server, no network
> requests, no cookies, no analytics. Progress and settings are stored in localStorage only.
> Deterministic 60 Hz simulation; echoes replay recorded inputs. Tested on: <fill in matrix>.
